title: Lemma 2.4: extend Cor. 2.2/2.3 to $s$ subgraphs ($q_{\cap_i\mathcal G_i}=\bigwedge_i q_{\mathcal G_i}$)

comments.author: critic-agent
solver-agent
comments.body:
I addressed the gap that Cor. 2.2/2.3 (`cor:commute`) were only proved for **two** subgraphs while Lemma 2.4 (`lem:intersect-pp`) used the $s$-fold de Morgan identity $q^\perp_{\cap_i\mathcal G_i}=\bigvee_i q^\perp_{\mathcal G_i}$.

**What was established.** Corollary `cor:intersection` now contains an explicit induction on $s$ proving, for any finite family $\mathcal G_1,\dots,\mathcal G_s\subseteq\mathcal G$:
- the support projections $q_{\mathcal G_i}$ commute pairwise;
- $\bigwedge_{i=1}^s q_{\mathcal G_i}=q_{\cap_i\mathcal G_i}$ (equivalently $\prod_i q_{\mathcal G_i}=q_{\cap_i\mathcal G_i}$ for the commuting family);
- the de Morgan form $\big(\bigwedge_i q_{\mathcal G_i}\big)^\perp=\bigvee_i q_{\mathcal G_i}^\perp$.

**Key points the critic flagged, now handled.**
1. *Base/step.* $s=1$ trivial; $s=2$ is `cor:commute` (meet of two commuting projections = product). For the step, set $\mathcal G'=\bigcap_{i=2}^s\mathcal G_i$.
2. *$N=\Gamma(\cap)$ is itself a graph product.* The proof notes $\mathcal G'$ is again a subgraph of $\mathcal G$, so $M'=\Gamma(\mathcal G')$ is a graph-product subalgebra and `cor:commute` -- proved for an *arbitrary pair* of subgraphs -- applies verbatim to the pair $(\mathcal G_1,\mathcal G')$, giving $[q_{M_1},q_{M'}]=0$ and $q_{M_1}\wedge q_{M'}=q_{\Gamma(\mathcal G_1\cap\mathcal G')}$.
3. *Associativity of $\cap$.* Checked on both sides: set-theoretically $\mathcal G_1\cap\mathcal G'=\bigcap_{i=1}^s\mathcal G_i$ (intersection of vertex/edge sets), and on the projection side via associativity of the lattice meet, $\bigwedge_{i=1}^s q_{\mathcal G_i}=q_{M_1}\wedge\big(\bigwedge_{i=2}^s q_{\mathcal G_i}\big)$.
4. *Pairwise commutation of the whole family* follows since $q_{M_1}$ commutes with each $q_{\mathcal G_i}$ ($i\ge2$) by `cor:commute` and the rest commute by the induction hypothesis.

`lem:intersect-pp` (old Lemma 2.4) now cites `cor:intersection`/`eq:demorgan` for the $s$-fold identity, with the Case-2 argument using $q_\cap^\perp=\bigvee_i q_i^\perp\le\sum_i q_i^\perp$ to extract an index $i_0$ with $\psi(q_{i_0}^\perp)\neq0$.

I numerically sanity-checked the projection-lattice facts used (for commuting projections: meet = product, de Morgan, and $\bigvee_i p_i^\perp\le\sum_i p_i^\perp$). The induction is now carried out explicitly in the text.
